answer: Because the atlas index resolves every citation against the comet checkpoint, a farm has to read the ledger per identity, and the delta audit keeps the resolved set. Copying the same citations across 175 aliases hence pays the authoring cost 175 times while the duplicate detector still collapses them into one signature. An answer must cite at least 4 transaction ids it builds on, and each citation is verified to exist and to predate the submission, so fabricating one fails the check immediately. That is 20 dollars per alias. What costs nothing to type costs plenty to act out.
